How to use the app, step by step.
Clip margins and subtitle style are in the player menu.
A notification when cards are waiting for review.
Notifications are off for this app. Allow them in the phone\'s settings to get the reminder.

Helat Player is a video player for learning a language from films. While you watch, save the lines you want to learn: each one becomes a card with its audio, a picture from the film, the text and your meaning. Then review the cards a little every day until you know them.

• Open file: choose a video or audio file on your phone. You can also open a video from another app with \"Open with\".\n• Paste link: play a direct link or stream URL (http:// or https://). The app warns you before it opens an unencrypted http:// link.\n• Videos continue where you left them. The last one is at the top of the home screen; older ones are under Recently played. The ✕ removes one; Clear history removes all of them (your cards are kept).

• Most MKV and WebM films have subtitle tracks inside. Choose one with Subtitles in the player menu.
• Load subtitle file: use an .srt or .vtt file from your phone instead. It then appears at the top of the Subtitles list; choosing another track or turning subtitles off puts it away (load it again to bring it back).
• Subtitle style: choose the colour and size. Built-in tracks use the new style the next time you open a video.
• Saved lines take their text and exact times from the subtitles, so a film with subtitles gives the best cards. If the film also has a Persian track, it fills in the meaning.

Tap the video to show or hide the controls. They stay while your finger is on the screen and hide 4 seconds after you let go.
• ‹ Line and Line › jump to the start of the previous or next subtitle line (in the pause after a line, ‹ Line plays that line again). If that line is more than 10 seconds away, they move 5 seconds. With subtitles off or without subtitles they are −5s and +5s. The bar below shows where you are.
• Repeat plays the current line again.
• The small loop button at the side repeats the current line until you tap it again, seek, or reach the end. It lights up at once; on online films finding the line can take a moment.
• Search subtitles: type a word or part of a line to list every line that has it; tap one to play the film from there. The first search of a film reads all its subtitles (online, only if the file indexes them; otherwise load an SRT file).
• Speed: 1×, 0.75×, 0.5× or 1.25×. Slower speech is easier to follow.
• Aspect changes how the picture fits the screen; Audio chooses the sound track.
• The player turns with the phone, and landscape is full screen. Full screen and Portrait lock one direction; Auto-rotate unlocks it.

When you hear a sentence you want to learn, use the small bookmark button at the side of the video.
• Tap: the line is saved in the background and the film keeps playing. A short message says Saved, with Undo for a moment.
• Hold: the film pauses and an editor opens. Check the start and end times (Preview plays them), the text, the meaning and the picture. Text from switches between subtitle tracks.

Where the times and text come from, in this order:
1. A subtitle file you loaded.
2. A subtitle track inside the video (MKV or WebM).
3. Without subtitles, the pauses in speech around the moment are found on the phone. The card then has no text; you can type it in the editor.

Clip margins (player menu) keep a little audio before and after each line, so the first and last words are not cut off.

Cards live in five boxes (the Leitner system). New cards start in Box 1.
• Box 1 comes up every day, Box 2 every 2 days, Box 3 every 4, Box 4 every 8 and Box 5 every 16.
• Start review on the home screen shows the cards due today. The audio plays first, while the picture, text and meaning are blurred. Listen, try to understand, then tap each part (or Show all) to check.
• Say it records you saying the line; it stops when you pause. Mine plays your voice, Mine + original plays yours and then the film's. The recording is deleted when you go to the next card.
• I knew it moves the card up one box. Didn't know sends it back to Box 1.
• Speed (next to Play again) plays the card slower: 1×, 0.75× or 0.5×. The choice is kept.
• Browse cards shows every box. The search field above them finds cards in all boxes by text, meaning or film. Open a card to play it, edit its text and meaning, or delete it.

Say the lines of a scene in turn with the actor.
1. Pause where the scene starts and choose Role-play in the player menu.
2. Choose the scene: a number of lines from now, or a time range (From and To, as m:ss; Now fills in the current time; at most 10 minutes). Choose who starts, and tap a line to change who says it.
3. Pause the film on my lines: the film waits until you finish speaking. Turn it off to keep the film going in real time.
4. On your lines the film goes quiet and your voice is recorded. Done ends your turn; Skip leaves the line to the actor.
5. At the end, Play my scene plays the scene without pauses, with your voice in place of the actor's. Compare line by line plays the actor's line and yours.

Role-play needs subtitles and the microphone. Use headphones so the film is not recorded with your voice. Recordings stay on the phone and are deleted when you close role-play.

Cards are kept only on this phone; uninstalling the app deletes them.
• Back up (home screen) saves all cards, with their audio and pictures, in one ZIP file wherever you choose, for example Google Drive.
• Restore adds the cards from such a file. Cards that are already here are skipped.
• If there has been no backup for 14 days, the home screen reminds you. ✕ hides the reminder for a week.

The backup also lists the links of the videos the cards came from, so keep it private.

• Language (Settings on the home screen): the phone's language, English or Persian. Cards and subtitles are not translated.
• Daily review reminder (Settings): a notification at the time you choose (20:00 at first) when cards are due. Android asks to allow notifications when you turn it on.
• Clip margins (player menu): how much audio is kept before and after each saved line, from 0 to 1.5 seconds. Applies to the next lines you save.
• Subtitle style (player menu): colour and size of subtitles, also used for the text on cards.
• About (Settings): the version, who made the app and a link to GitHub.

• Use headphones for role-play and when you listen closely.
• Watch with subtitles in the language you are learning; a Persian track fills in the meaning.
• Save fewer but useful lines, and review a little every day.
• For online films, a direct link to an MKV file works best: its subtitle tracks are read from the link too. A slow connection makes saving slower.
• For hard sentences, lower the speed and use the loop button.

• Sound but a black picture: go back and open the video again.
• "VLC could not play this media": the file may be damaged or the link may have expired. Try it in another player.
• "No line found": there are no text subtitles near that moment and no clear speech was found. Hold the save button and set the times by hand.
• The times are a little off: hold the button and adjust them, or change Clip margins.
• Subtitles inside MP4 files and picture subtitles (PGS, VobSub) cannot be read as text. Load an .srt file instead.
• The app runs on 64-bit phones only.
